messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: GPU_VRAM_EVICTION on prod-cluster-3 at 1918000000. Affected service: text-gen-api. Paging @eng-oncall.
infra-bot: Auto-attach: node=node-3b7b, pod=text-gen-2, event=oom_kill, vram_used=94%. Logs: `OOMKilled` x3 in 10m.
maya: acknowledged — I'm on it. moving to incident channel. starting triage.
maya: quick check — are these new models or higher batch sizes? anyone changed rollout?
jon: no recent rollouts in the window. saw a small spike in sustained seq_len for a few clients (~3k tokens) — could be a customer job.
sam: if it's sustained tokens + batching, VRAM can spike. suggested immediate mitigations: 1) reduce batch size on prod router for text-gen-api, 2) cordon node-3b7b, 3) scale up fallback pool.
maya: doing 1 now — scaling router batch_max_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 (will affect latency but prevent OOMs).
maya: cordon/drain node-3b7b — `kubectl cordon node-3b7b` then `kubectl drain node-3b7b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
infra-bot: drain started. evictions in progress. moving pods to node-3c1a.
leo: started an emergency scale on dedicated-gpu-pool: +2 machines (NVIDIA A100) to give headroom.
irene: adding a temporary alert silence for ECC_ALERT high-frequency to avoid noise during mitigation: `POST /api/alerts/silence {service: ECC_ALERT, duration: 1h}`
jon: seeing VRAM headroom metric drop on node-3c1a too — might be global workload shift. attaching histogram for vram_usage_percent for last 30m.
sam: ok, if traffic remains high we should enable automatic prefix cache for long sequences (enable kv-cache policy) and set per-request token cap for long-running requests.
maya: customer-impact: some requests were 502/timeout during evictions. support already got a handful of tickets. advised SLA risk but service still responding to lower-batch requests.
leo: drain finished. node-3b7b out of rotation. infra will run thermal/ECC diagnostics offline.
irene: thermal sensors show occasional spike coinciding with ECC bursts — flagging hardware team. but for short term: propose reducing pager severity for single ECC events -> `warning` unless >5 events/min or accompanied by OOM.
sam: agreed. also propose new alert: `vram_headroom_pct < 8% for 2m` -> page, current rule pages at 5% for 30s which is too noisy.
jon: I can draft the alert rules. proposal snippets:
```
- alert: VRAMHeadroomLow
  expr: 100 - avg_over_time(vram_usage_percent[2m]) < 8
  for: 2m
  severity: page
```
```
- alert: ECCBurst
  expr: increase(ecc_errors_total[1m]) > 5
  for: 1m
  severity: page
  # single events become `warning`
```
maya: plan for after-action: 1) update oncall playbook with new thresholds and runbook for draining, 2) add VRAM headroom panel to infra dashboard, 3) add ECC burst rate panel and rate-limit alert noise, 4) follow up with hw team on node-3b7b thermal logs.
sam: I'll add the dashboard panels and alert PR. tagging @jon for rule review.
jon: will review and push to staging alert rules. will also add an automated mute for alerts during node-drain job with label `drain=true`.
maya: thanks team. postmortem + action items: create incident ticket, assign hardware investigation to @leo, alert tuning to @jon/@sam, playbook edits to me. closing pager in 20m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged closed by maya at 1918003600 (status: mitigated, customer-impact: degraded, tickets: 4).
